gloss: to fold back; to turn back; to call back

definitions.gloss: to fold back; to turn up
definitions.explanation: To fold something back on itself, such as a hem or edge of fabric or paper.

definitions.gloss: to turn back; to retrace one's steps
definitions.explanation: To reverse direction and go back the way one came.

definitions.gloss: to call back; to reply promptly
definitions.explanation: To return a phone call or respond to a message. Very common in business contexts.

examples.japanese: ズボンの{裾|すそ}を{少|すこ}し{折|お}り{返|かえ}して{履|は}いている。
examples.english: I'm wearing my pants with the hems rolled up a little.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}の{端|はし}を{折|お}り{返|かえ}して{目印|めじるし}にした。
examples.english: I folded back the edge of the paper as a bookmark.

examples.japanese: {頂上|ちょうじょう}で{折|お}り{返|かえ}す。
examples.english: To turn back at the summit.

examples.japanese: マラソンの{折|お}り{返|かえ}し{地点|ちてん}を{過|す}ぎた。
examples.english: I passed the marathon's turnaround point.

examples.japanese: {途中|とちゅう}で{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}したので{折|お}り{返|かえ}した。
examples.english: It started raining on the way, so I turned back.

examples.japanese: {折|お}り{返|かえ}しお{電話|でんわ}します。
{担当者|たんとうしゃ}から{折|お}り{返|かえ}し{連絡|れんらく}いたします。
examples.english: The person in charge will get back to you.

examples.japanese: {留守番|るすばん}{電話|でんわ}にメッセージが{入|はい}っていたので、{折|お}り{返|かえ}し{電話|でんわ}をかけた。
examples.english: There was a message on the answering machine, so I called back.

notes:
A compound verb from {折|お}る (to fold) + {返|かえ}す (to return). The physical meaning of folding back extends metaphorically to turning around and to returning communication.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {折|お}り{返|かえ}し{電話|でんわ}する: to call back
- {折|お}り{返|かえ}し{連絡|れんらく}する: to get back in touch
- {折|お}り{返|かえ}し{地点|ちてん}: turnaround point
- {裾|すそ}を{折|お}り{返|かえ}す: to fold back the hem

USAGE:
The adverbial form {折|お}り{返|かえ}し (immediately, in return) is extremely common in business Japanese, especially in phone conversations: {折|お}り{返|かえ}しお{電話|でんわ}します (I'll call you right back). This is one of the most important business phrases for learners to know.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive in sense 1 (folding something back). Can be used intransitively in sense 2 (turning back oneself).
